_doc: Catalog-frame manifest for the {{TOOL_CATALOG}} placeholder. Source
of truth for the prose that frames the C++ renderer in
`api/catalog/prompt_section_renderer.cc`.
Each top-level key names a section the renderer emits; the value is
an `@file:<path>` reference to the .md file that holds the section
verbatim. No composition, no per-tool aggregation — the .md is what
the LLM sees. The codegen resolver in `generate.py` expands the
references and embeds each as a constexpr `std::string_view` in
`tool_catalog_frame.gen.h`.
Phase 13.9 finalized the flattening (started for `browser_tools` in
13.8 and extended to file/task/skill/parallelism here). Previously
each section was an object with per-piece fields (header / intro /
outro / body / read_before_edit_rule / groups) that the C++ side
composed with per-tool bullets aggregated from each *.tool.json's
`prompt` block. The codegen + renderer composition logic was deleted
along with `kPromptToolEntries`. Adding a new tool to the catalog
is now: drop the .tool.json AND edit the relevant section .md by
hand. The per-tool filtering at render time is gone — sessions that
enable any tool in a category see the whole section.
Section gating: each `Build<X>Section` in the renderer decides
whether to emit its content based on which tools are enabled.
Browser tools: any tool in `kBrowserToolWireNames` enabled.
File/shell tools: any tool in `kFileShellToolWireNames` enabled.
Task tracking: TodoWrite enabled. Skills: Skill enabled.
Parallelism: always emitted as a trailer when any other section is.
Companion to `system-prompt-tools.md` (which fills the separate
{{system-prompt-tools}} placeholder). Both feed the same C++
renderer; codegen emits `tool_catalog_frame.gen.h` whose constexpr
string_views are referenced by `prompt_section_renderer.cc`.
